main_text.p: mutarunt sententiam (quia exivantibus, aut lædentibus, non solum cognoscuntur interni morbi, sed curādi indicationes sumuntur)& ad cardiaca intus & foris adhibenda, quæ tunc ipsi misero ægrotanti convenire putabant, mox confugerunt, ex quibus tamen nullum quoq; cōmodum pror-sus percepit.Quinimò ijs potius, ut per hieram commemorata symptomata, cum vitalis facultatis & animalis in signi laesione intendebantur.Itaq; cùm prorsus nihil dormire posset, tandem miser ill[?] interij:qua-doquidem ad animalium vitam conserua-dam apprimè utilis est somnus. Post sectu est cadauer, in quo pancreas, integro saluo quæ vitæ principio, & stomacho, duntaxat compertum est abscessu putrefactum, unde per somnum spiritibus ab extremis par-tibus ad sua revocatis principia, tetros malignosq; vapores cor ferientes, & (forte) etiam stomachum efferri, excitariq; medici posthac coniectarunt. Unde nam autem ex crementicij humores, ex quibus illic excitatus fuerat abscessus promanarent, scire haud arduum est.Nam pancreas corpus es-se glandulosum primis lumborum verte-bris infidens, quòd quidem venarum &ac teria-

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "ill[?]" and "interij" in the line "miser illinterij:" are blurred by a smudge, so the middle word is doubtful. The phrase "&ac teria-" at the foot of the page is read as printed but the joined word is uncertain; it continues on the next page. Long s is printed as f throughout and has been normalised to s. "exivantibus" and "conseruā-" are normalised for u/v as required. No catchword or signature is visible.
